Orient the split along the short axis so the mass can open a usable court toward the access side.
Introduce a meaningful gap to register a public void rather than a sealed block.
Maintain continuity across the split while preserving a legible void beneath/through the mass.
Add a courtyard macro to carve an inhabitable public void from the dominant mass.
Size the courtyard to remain programmatic and not merely decorative.
Open the court to the verified access side for a stronger public threshold.

Shift the dominant break earlier so the lower mass becomes a more legible base and the upper volume can read as a calmer support/overhang.
Increase horizontal reach of the split gesture to make the public void and upper hierarchy more explicit.
Add a true carved public void to replace the current vague subtraction and strengthen neighborhood-living ground publicness.
Use a moderate court margin so the void remains usable rather than decorative.
Align the court opening to the program access side to improve frontage legibility and active threshold.

rationale: The candidate reads as a compact stepped/twisted block with some hierarchy, but the dominant gesture is not convincingly tied to neighborhood-living semantics. Across views it remains mostly a sealed, blocky mass with a sloped/terraced top, while the ground condition does not clearly open toward the verified access edge. The blue frontage is adjacent in all views, but the mass does not produce a strong court, notch, undercut, or entry seam on that side; instead the public response is weak and semantically vague. The form is coherent enough as a single object, but the silhouette feels more like an arbitrary stacked wedge than a capacity-aware mixed-use building with an active threshold. Reference 1 and 2 support the idea of a carved interior/public void; reference 3 reinforces a calm commercial ground edge; reference 5 is counterfactual and suggests a transferable bridge/void projection, but it does not match the current typology. Overall this fails program_fit_hard_pass because the visible mass does not adequately express active ground publicness or a clear section logic for neighborhood living.

warnings: Visible multi-view coherence is limited; the object reads best in iso/front but weakens in the opposite/top views.
The access edge response is too sealed; no clearly legible public threshold is formed on the frontage side.
The stepped/twisted upper gesture does not currently earn a strong programmatic reason and risks reading as arbitrary.
Parcel containment appears acceptable, but containment alone is not sufficient to pass program fit.
